rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28)
binary: rustc
commit-hash: b940084d7eb6a299eb4bfeb8e34901bc051e7ac4
commit-date: 2026-09-28
host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
release: 1.99.0
LLVM version: 23.1.1
reviewNotes: Hosted CI run 37112635227 at commit 1a68553b generated the actual native linker maps and canonical input listings using the pinned official rust:1.99.0-bookworm image (index SHA-256 59037199c44290f2befcdd58dcc540164763fc296950255aaefeef096a1866b0). The probe used profile ci: opt-level 3, LTO disabled, codegen-units 16; it was not a fat-LTO release validation. Every listing hashes to its candidate fingerprint, and all exported standard-library notice bytes match the listing. Reviewed the complete Rust 1.99.0 standard-library aggregate and all twelve standalone sysroot license texts. The standalone texts, in-tree notices and retained component notice bodies are unchanged from 1.98.1; dependency versions changed without new license expressions, and libc author metadata changed in the upstream aggregate. Preserve that complete aggregate and every notice/exception; compiler implementation dependencies remain outside the inventory. The hosted Windows TUI maps retain the fourteen previously reviewed native paths and eleven system DLL imports. dpkg evidence confirms gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64-win32 12.2.0-14+deb12u1+25.2+b1 (win32 thread model) and mingw-w64-x86-64-dev 10.0.0-3 from the pinned Debian snapshot. The maps contain crt2.o, crtbegin.o/crtend.o, libmingw32/libmingwex runtime members, system import stubs, libgcc _ctors.o and libgcc_eh unwind-seh.o; no winpthreads member is present. libbcrypt.a remains SHA-256 8bfab23499133842d4b2abc75d13687791b03a1e5ad403b62c5894cbe633dd5c; BCryptGenRandom is an import trampoline to bcrypt.dll, covered by mingw-w64 10.0.0 ZPL-2.1 attribution. The SystemFunction036 fallback uses ADVAPI32.dll. Retain the mingw-w64 copyright/ZPL-2.1 terms and disclaimer, and the GCC GPLv3 notices with GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1 for linked libgcc objects. Windows system DLLs are not bundled. Actual reviewed builds still compare their native/import closure to this allowlist; another compiler, builder or changed fingerprint requires review.
description: Rust 1.99.0 standard-library notices and Debian Bookworm mingw-w64 runtime/startup attribution for Windows. mingw-w64 startup/runtime/import-library objects and GCC runtime objects are statically linked; Windows system DLLs are not bundled. Limited to the fingerprinted x86_64-w64-mingw32 cross inputs of the pinned official rust:1.99.0-bookworm builder.

Preserve that complete aggregate and every notice/exception; compiler implementation dependencies remain outside the inventory. Their maps link rcrt1.o, crti.o/crtn.o, crtbeginS.o/crtendS.o, libc.a and libunwind.a, with no imported system library; no GCC startup/runtime object is linked from the Debian driver. Rust 1.99.0 src/ci/docker/scripts/musl.sh pins musl 1.2.5 with the CVE-2025-26519, CVE-2026-6042 and CVE-2026-40200 patches; hosted native .comment evidence reports GCC 9.4.0. LLVM libunwind and compiler-rt startup source provenance is Rust 1.99.0's src/llvm-project submodule 1b9c0d5ff9bbe7634aead059efe6b11a7eeba145. Its exact libunwind/compiler-rt LICENSE.TXT bytes were inspected and remain identical to the existing Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception notices; rust-notice-sources.json pins their new source commit and unchanged hashes, together with the musl MIT copyright. Preserve all these notices. The probe observed the startup selection after Rust 1.99's static-PIE support change; actual reviewed builds still validate their native/import closure, and another compiler, target, builder or changed fingerprint requires review.
description: Rust 1.99.0 standard-library, musl libc 1.2.5 and LLVM runtime notices for the static x86_64-unknown-linux-musl TUI and server. Rust's self-contained startup objects, libc.a and LLVM libunwind are linked; no system library is imported. Limited to the fingerprinted rustup target archives in the pinned official rust:1.99.0-bookworm builder.
